searchText: I have a side question for EOF regarding this. Things which we "ban" in EOF can still be reached from ETH*CALL instructions, so for instance if you want to use BLOCKHASH opcode instead of system call you can call into a legacy contract, and if you want an indication of how much GAS is left you can do the same. Unless I've missed anything EOF can call legacy contracts - right? Banning blockhash is for a different reason: to simplify the semantics of eof contracts. Implicit observation is always a thing, but you have to also consider call targets as a black box. They may revert due to gas observation or any other reasons. What removing gas observability ensures is that eof contracts themselves cant be broken by gas alone. Third party interactions are excluded from this promise.
